assertion.rationale: F1: data-api's middleware chain has a readOnlyGuard but no authentication layer in front of it, so external ingress meant any caller could execute any exposed transaction (feed reads, table scans) without being limited to a permitted set. F1 is now CLOSED (Task 6): infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep's dataApiApp module sets ingressExternal:false, so data-api's transactions are reachable only through the server-side nginx proxy inside the Container Apps environment — both frontends' nginx.conf.template already carried the /api/ proxy rule, verified present in both, so this closes the gap without adding a token to distribute or rotate. F13: zero workload RBAC exists in IaC — there is no principal-scoped restriction on which transactions or functions each workload identity may perform; the only grants that exist are subscription-scoped Owner (deployer) and Reader (verifier), an all-or-nothing shape with no per-function limitation for data-api, mcp-tools or cost-ingest. Task 12 expresses five of the seven documented grants in code — data-api and mcp-tools each get Log Analytics Reader (LAW scope) and Security Reader (subscription scope), mcp-tools gets Cost Management Reader, data-api's SQL contained-database user and Fabric workspace Viewer grants are expressed in data/seed/sql/900-contained-users.sql and infra/fabric/provision-workspace.ps1 respectively — scoped per transaction rather than left at the all-or-nothing Owner/Reader shape. Task 17 (F15, now CLOSED) expresses the sixth: layer-06-platform.yml now creates the cost export via `az rest` against the Exports REST API (api-version 2023-08-01) with an explicit `identity: { type: SystemAssigned }` request in the PUT body — the `az costmanagement` CLI extension has neither an --identity-type flag nor, at its pinned API version, any support for RBAC-only storage (it hard-requires shared keys, github.com/Azure/azure-cli/issues/32912) — and grants that identity's principalId Storage Blob Data Contributor, scoped to the cost-exports container, once the PUT response returns it. F13 is NOT fully closed: cost-ingest's Storage Blob Data Reader grant is blocked on F19 (cost-ingest has no Function App or identity anywhere in this repo's IaC). Overall status stays GAP: F1 is closed, and F13 is six-sevenths expressed, but the one remaining grant means transactions for cost-ingest are still not limited to authorized processes by construction. CORRECTION (2026-08-28, final pre-publication audit -- F25). The sentence above about Task 6 closing F1 was written from F1's own Fix text and was INCOMPLETE, and the clause it leaned on -- "both frontends already proxy /api/ server-side" -- was the bypass rather than the reason internal ingress sufficed. control-tower and launch-ops were themselves ingressExternal:true with NO authConfig, and both nginx.conf.template files blind-proxy `location /api/ { proxy_pass ${DATA_API_ORIGIN}/; }` with no credential and no path allowlist, so GET https://<control-tower-fqdn>/api/feeds/secure-score reached data-api unauthenticated from the public internet -- against an identity holding Security Reader at SUBSCRIPTION scope. F25 closes it: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep now puts Container Apps Easy Auth (entraEasyAuthConfig(), RedirectToLoginPage, an Entra provider with only a public clientId and openIdIssuer, tokenStore disabled, no client secret) in front of launch-ops, control-tower AND compliance, and each app's ingressExternal is the same expression as "is Easy Auth configured", so no parameter combination publishes one of them without authentication. excludedPaths is ['/healthz'] and nothing else, so nothing under /api/ is reachable without a session. .github/workflows/layer-07-apps.yml resolves MLS_LAUNCH_OPS_CLIENT_ID, MLS_CONTROL_TOWER_CLIENT_ID and MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID from the Entra app registrations L3 creates, treating a hand-set variable as an override; an ID it cannot resolve leaves that app internal-only rather than failing the deploy or publishing it open (F36 -- an earlier revision of this workflow refused to deploy at all without all three, which made the F25 fix undeployable out of the box, and is the claim this sentence used to carry). F26, found alongside it: the runbook's claim that an unset MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID made ARM reject the deployment was false -- an undefined GitHub variable expands to the EMPTY STRING, so readEnvironmentVariable returned '' and never reached its 'unset' default (reproduced against Bicep CLI 0.46.1); the guard now treats empty and 'unset' alike. Verified by verification/tests/frontend-auth.Tests.ps1 (14 assertions, each mutation-tested) and az bicep build; nothing has been deployed. CLOSED (2026-08-28, commit c33f06e -- F19, on explicit sponsor authorisation). F13's seventh and last documented grant -- cost-ingest -> Storage Blob Data Reader -- is now expressed in code. It could not be before: F19 meant apps/cost-ingest, a complete and tested Azure Functions app, appeared in no Bicep anywhere, so it had no Function App, no identity, and therefore no principal for the grant to be written against. infra/bicep/platform/main.bicep now provisions the Function App on a Flex Consumption (FC1) plan with a user-assigned identity, and grants that identity Storage Blob Data Reader (2a2b9908-6ea1-4ae2-8e65-a410df84e7d1) scoped to the cost-exports CONTAINER -- not the storage account and not the subscription -- via the new infra/bicep/platform/modules/blob-container-role.bicep. Flex Consumption is a least-privilege choice as much as a cost one: it is the only plan that supports a managed-identity AzureWebJobsStorage with no Azure Files shared-key connection string, so the Function introduces no stored credential (CLAUDE.md hard rule 5); and because that plan supports only the Event Grid-based blob trigger, the Function keeps no blob receipts or poison queue in the account it watches, which is what lets the grant there stay a pure read. The three account-wide roles the Functions host requires (Storage Blob Data Owner, Storage Queue Data Contributor, Storage Table Data Contributor) bind to a SECOND, empty runtime storage account created for that purpose, never to the cost-export account -- consolidating them would have handed the identity Owner-class blob access to the very container this grant narrows it to. Its OneLake write access is Fabric workspace Contributor (infra/fabric/provision-workspace.ps1, -CostIngestPrincipalId, wired from layer-07-apps.yml): Viewer is read-only and cannot create Files/cost_daily/, Contributor is the lowest of Fabric's four workspace roles that can write, and Fabric exposes no data-plane role narrower than the workspace -- it is the broadest grant any workload identity holds in this estate and is argued for at the grant itself. STATUS MOVES TO CLOSED because every finding this review raised against this control is now addressed -- F1 (Task 6, completed by F25/F26) and now F13 -- and CLOSED here means exactly what compliance/README.md's Register vocabulary says it means: no known open finding stands against this control. It is not a claim that the control is met, that the estate was assessed exhaustively, or that anything was verified against a live tenant. WHAT IS AND IS NOT VERIFIED. Nothing in this estate has ever been deployed; no Azure, Entra or Fabric call was made to build or test any of this. The evidence is repo-static -- it describes what the repository DECLARES. verification/tests/cost-ingest.Tests.ps1 (43 assertions) asserts the role definition GUID and the container scope against comment-stripped Bicep, never against comment text (the F27 ruling), refuses any role GUID outside the four this leg documents, and checks that the account-wide host roles bind only to the runtime storage account; infra/fabric/tests/provision-workspace.Tests.ps1 asserts the Fabric role string per principal. Three surgical mutations were run against those suites and each turned exactly the intended assertions red: widening the container grant to account scope (1 failure), dropping the user-assigned identity (1 failure), widening the Fabric role to Member (6 failures). STILL OUTSTANDING, and carried in the recommendation below rather than dropped: F13's Fix text also called for a V7.x audit criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles and no others. That does not exist. A live-tenant criterion has never had a tenant to assert against, and the static tests above guard what this repository declares, not what any subscription holds.

recommendation: No open finding remains against this control. Every workload identity's transactions are limited by an expressed grant scoped no wider than the role permits -- container scope for the cost-export read, workspace scope for the Log Analytics reads, subscription scope only for the two roles that have no narrower resource to bind to -- and data-api is reachable only from inside the Container Apps environment, behind authenticated frontends (Tasks 6, 12, 17, F24, F25, F26 and F19). STILL OUTSTANDING: add a V7.x Verifier criterion asserting that each workload principal holds exactly its expected roles at exactly its expected scopes, and no others, read back from ARM as mls-verifier. All seven grants are now expressed in IaC and guarded by static tests over this repository, but no criterion has ever compared that declaration against a deployed tenant -- because nothing has ever been deployed.
